Consult Summary:
- 5-day history of dry cough and persistent rhinorrhea with intermittent chills/feeling hot; no dyspnea or chest pain; likely viral respiratory infection; advised symptomatic care, temperature monitoring, and safety-netting. Past history of diabetes and hypertension on metformin and lisinopril.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dry cough every 20–30 minutes and constantly streaming nose for ~5 days.
- Timeline: Onset ~5 days ago; diarrhea at onset (resolved). Symptoms ongoing; Lemsip provides temporary throat soothing.
- Associated symptoms: Feeling hot with chills; myalgias; green nasal discharge.
- Pertinent negatives: No sputum production, chest pain, shortness of breath, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, epistaxis, rash, headache, or visual changes. No current vomiting or diarrhea. No sinus tenderness reported.
- Oral intake: Eating and drinking adequately; tolerating fluids; normal urination.
- Fever: No thermometer used; subjective fever/chills reported.
- Baseline respiratory history: No chronic chest problems; exertional wheeze only with intense exercise.
- Recent care: Patient reports a diabetes-related blood test ~3 weeks ago was “normal” (specific test not documented).

Past Medical History:
- Diabetes mellitus (type not specified)
  - Background: Reports recent blood test “normal” ~3 weeks ago.
  - Monitoring: Does not have/uses no home blood glucose monitoring equipment.
  - Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Hypertension
  - Control: Last BP check “a while ago,” stability unknown.
  - Medications: Lisinopril; patient stated dose “200” (dose likely inaccurate; route/frequency not documented; conflict noted).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.
- Seasonal/environmental: Hay fever, mild.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with partner and a dog.
- Occupation: Office manager.
- Alcohol: Occasional use (“the odd cherry” — type/amount unclear).
- Tobacco: Smoking status not documented.
- Other substances: Not documented.

Family History:
- Not mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- General/other: No in-visit examination findings documented.
- Anthropometrics (self-reported): Height 5 ft 5 in; Weight 65 kg.

Investigations:
- Patient-reported diabetes-related blood test ~3 weeks ago “normal” (specific test and values not documented).
- No other labs or imaging performed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute cough with rhinorrhea, likely viral respiratory infection
  - Assessment: 5 days of dry cough and green nasal discharge; no dyspnea, chest pain, or hemoptysis; tolerating PO; subjective fever/chills without measured temperature. Diabetes increases risk for bacterial superinfection.
  - Plan:
    - Purchase and use a thermometer; monitor temperature.
    - Supportive care: Continue Lemsip (contains paracetamol/acetaminophen). Avoid taking other paracetamol/acetaminophen-containing products concurrently.
    - Cough management: Avoid daytime cough suppressants; may use small amount of cough syrup at night if cough prevents sleep.
    - Hydration and rest.
    - Safety-netting: Seek re-evaluation if temperature persists >37.5–38°C, if cough worsens, if purulent sputum develops, hemoptysis, significant epistaxis, shortness of breath, or chest pain. Antibiotics may be considered if symptoms worsen or fever persists.
- Issue 2: Diabetes mellitus
  - Assessment: No acute hyperglycemic symptoms; no home glucose monitoring; recent test reportedly “normal.”
  - Plan:
    - Continue metformin as prescribed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Ensure routine diabetes follow-up with primary care as scheduled.
    - Maintain hydration during illness; monitor for any increase in urination/thirst or other hyperglycemia symptoms.
- Issue 3: Hypertension
  - Assessment: On lisinopril; dose stated as “200” (likely inaccurate).
  - Plan:
    - Continue lisinopril as prescribed; verify correct dose and regimen with pharmacy/GP.
    - Arrange routine blood pressure check with primary care.

General plan items:
- Return/seek care promptly if red-flag symptoms occur as above.
- No antibiotics prescribed at this time.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Objective vitals (including temperature, BP, HR, SpO2), lung exam, detailed medication doses/routes/frequencies (metformin, lisinopril), smoking status, immunization status (e.g., influenza, pneumococcal), home glucose monitoring plan, allergy confirmation beyond patient report, past surgical history, family history.
- Internal conflicts: Lisinopril dose reported as “200” (outside typical dosing range) — likely inaccurate; conflict noted. Alcohol detail unclear (“the odd cherry”).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor omissions/interruptions and a few unclear phrases (smoking question unanswered; some audio gaps).
